question_candidates.stop_reason: Sourced review answers the Candidate's discriminator instead of leaving it open. updateAttributes only raises the dependency components it is given, starting from the deps vector carried in the message and skipping the row of the instance owner named in that message, so a pre-accepting peer returns a vector that dominates the leader's transmitted vector componentwise. With one counted peer (N=3, Thrifty, FastQuorumSize-1 = 1) the leader's componentwise merge therefore equals that peer's vector in every compared component, and mergeAttributes ignores only the leader's own row. In an owner-led instance the peer skips exactly that row, so the merged vector equals the peer's record and the fast-commit branch installs the same vector on the leader: both members of the fast quorum hold the committed vector at the same vbal, and any recovery quorum the recoverer can assemble (self plus one reply, with both remaining replicas being fast-quorum members) contains a holder. That mechanism is what keeps the exemption from publishing an unsupported vector, so the proposition is explained. The surviving exposure is confined to one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes keeps the leader's own row value while the peer may have raised it; it requires the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader, and it is recorded as the remaining premise. The map is updated in the same product (B4's unknown and the N<=3 open detail) so the earlier, over-broad phrasing does not mislead the next question.

question.question: handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal for instance (Replica, Instance) and never writes inst.Status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept holds accepted attributes with Status NONE, and one that did see it keeps PREACCEPTED or PREACCEPTED_EQ. Does any decision depend on an accepted record carrying status ACCEPTED: can a later PreAccept for the same instance overwrite the accepted attributes because handlePreAccept's >= ACCEPTED guard cannot fire, and can a recovery that should re-accept an already accepted value instead take the phase-1 restart path because handlePrepareReply's sub-case 2 needs a reply whose Status is ACCEPTED?
question.importance: An acceptor that stores accepted attributes without recording that it accepted them can (a) have those attributes recomputed by a later PreAccept at the same or a higher ballot instead of being preserved, and (b) hide from a recovering leader the fact that the value reached the accept phase, which is the distinction between re-proposing the accepted value and starting a fresh phase 1. Either effect can change the value a majority eventually commits for the instance, which is agreement-relevant rather than cosmetic; the accept phase is also the only place where a value is fixed without commands being stored, so a wrong reconstruction can also drop a command that only some replicas hold.

selections.rationale: First substantive product of this run: a partial but usable map of the EPaxos replica responsibility (core_overview for both core relationships, seven activities, sixteen behaviors, seven facts, ten surfaced unread boundaries) plus the first Candidate. The map is sourced only from the captured snapshot; all anomalies found while tracing the backbone are retained as open_details instead of being asserted as defects. The Candidate selects the one sourced discrepancy that would matter most if reachable: handlePreAccept stores a received command into InstanceSpace[PreAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler addresses the instance (PreAccept.Replica, Instance) named by the message.

after.purpose: Form a per-instance decision: fix the command, its sequence number and its dependency vector, and advance the instance from tentative pre-accept through accept to commit.
after.realization_summary: handlePropose allocates (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq,deps) from the local conflict tables, records the instance as PREACCEPTED and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers (Thrifty). handlePreAccept recomputes attributes on the receiver and replies with (bal,vbal,seq,deps,CommittedUpTo,status). handlePreAcceptReply merges replies and commits on the fast path when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and allEqual and (for N>7) allCommitted and the ballot is the initial ballot; otherwise the instance moves to ACCEPTED and a majority accept round runs in handleAcceptReply (acceptOKs+1 > N/2), followed by bcastCommit.

after.purpose: Carry the per-instance authority context: which ballot the record is promised to, at which ballot its attributes were last fixed, and which replica may currently advance it.
after.realization_summary: Each Instance keeps bal (highest ballot promised) and vbal (ballot at which the current attributes were established). maxRecvBallot is raised by every received message type and constrains makeBallot, which picks id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and further raised while IsLeader. Ballot comparison gates every message and reply: lower ballots are dropped or nacked, and a majority of nacks lets a replica raise the ballot and run prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead it does.

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

selections.rationale: Feedback-only product that narrows the active Candidate's exposure using source structure, without changing any map object. Comparing how the leader's and the peer's dependency vectors are computed shows why the N<=3 Thrifty equality exemption is sound in the owner-led case and why the recovery-led case is the one that can split: a peer recomputes with updateAttributes starting from the leader's transmitted deps vector and only increases components, and it skips the instance owner's row, so with a single fast-quorum peer the merged vector (componentwise maximum) equals that peer's vector whenever the leader is also the owner, and the leader installs that same merged vector on commit. When the leader is not the owner (recovery sub-case 5/6 restarts phase 1 for another replica's instance), the leader and the peer each skip the owner's row but add their own knowledge to their own rows, so the leader can contribute a component on the leader's row that the peer lacks while the peer contributes one on a different row: the merged vector is then strictly greater than both records and is held only by the leader after its fast commit.

feedback.answered: The exemption's reachable window is now located on sources. updateAttributes only raises the dependency components it is given: it starts from the received deps vector, skips the row of the instance owner named in the message, and for every other row raises deps[q] to the highest conflicting instance known locally (S7-attributes). A pre-accepting peer therefore returns a vector that dominates the leader's transmitted vector componentwise; with one peer (N=3, Thrifty, FastQuorumSize-1 = 1) the leader's merge equals that peer's vector, and the fast-commit branch installs the merged vector into the leader's own record (S10-handlePreAcceptReply). formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

question.importance: Wrong-slot attribution of a command mutates protocol state without any quorum behind it: a record that never committed that command can become executable as though it had, while the record the message was addressed to can be left permanently unexecutable because executeCommands requires Cmds != nil and findSCC returns false for a command-less instance. Both effects are consensus-visible (an uncommitted command can reach the state machine, and a committed instance can stop making progress).

compare the record that receives Cmds after the handler returns against the record named by (Replica, Instance)

The wrong-slot write at epaxos/epaxos.go:809 assigns the received command to InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance], but every other access in handlePreAccept addresses the instance named by the message, (preAccept.Replica, preAccept.Instance). question.question: handlePreAcceptReply commits when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and inst.lb.allEqual && allCommitted && isInitialBallot, but for r.N <= 3 with Thrifty the reply-wise equality result is discarded (the allEqual accumulator is never updated), so with N = 3 the leader fast-commits its own (seq, deps) after a single reply whose recomputed attributes may differ. Can such a commit leave two attribute vectors for one instance at the same vbal -- the leader's committed vector and the fast-quorum peer's pre-accepted vector -- so that a later recovery, which selects the reply with the highest vbal by iterating the reply slice with element.VBallot >= lb.ballot, can adopt the peer's vector instead of the committed one; and does the legal crash point between the leader's local fast commit and bcastCommit make that reachable while some replica has already executed the committed vector?
question.importance: If reachable, one instance is committed with different (seq, deps) at different replicas, so the same command is ordered differently against conflicting commands on different replicas; execution then applies the same commands in different orders, the surviving replicas' state diverges, and a reply already produced under the old order is contradicted. That is a consensus-safety consequence (agreement and state-machine convergence), not a performance or liveness one.

recovering replica that later runs prepare for the instance

peer recomputes d2 != d1 (or s2 != s1) against its own conflict index and replies PREACCEPTED

recoverer runs prepare and selects the candidate value among replies with element.VBallot >= lb.ballot
compare the (Seq, Deps) the recoverer re-commits with the vector the leader committed

question.trigger_rationale: The exemption is explicit in the source: in handlePreAcceptReply the equality result computed by mergeAttributes is only accumulated in the else branch, so for r.N <= 3 && r.Thrifty inst.lb.allEqual keeps its initial true value from newLeaderBookkeeping (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S2-instance-bookkeeping). With FastQuorumSize = F + (F+1)/2 = 2 for N = 3 (S21-quorum-sizes) and the commit condition preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1, one disagreeing reply is enough to commit the leader's own vector. The candidate pairs the commit with the recovery rule that must reconstruct the same value: handlePrepareReply keeps the attributes of the reply with the highest vbal (S15-handlePrepareReply), so two vectors at one vbal are the discriminator. A controlled multi-replica schedule is the check that could distinguish an actual same-vbal split from the author's intended majority-intersection argument.

question.question: handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal for instance (Replica, Instance) and never writes inst.Status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept holds accepted attributes with Status NONE, and one that did see it keeps PREACCEPTED or PREACCEPTED_EQ. Does any decision depend on an accepted record carrying status ACCEPTED: can a later PreAccept for the same instance overwrite the accepted attributes because handlePreAccept's >= ACCEPTED guard cannot fire, and can a recovery that should re-accept an already accepted value instead take the phase-1 restart path because handlePrepareReply's sub-case 2 needs a reply whose Status is ACCEPTED?
question.importance: An acceptor that stores accepted attributes without recording that it accepted them can (a) have those attributes recomputed by a later PreAccept at the same or a higher ballot instead of being preserved, and (b) hide from a recovering leader the fact that the value reached the accept phase, which is the distinction between re-proposing the accepted value and starting a fresh phase 1. Either effect can change the value a majority eventually commits for the instance, which is agreement-relevant rather than cosmetic; the accept phase is also the only place where a value is fixed without commands being stored, so a wrong reconstruction can also drop a command that only some replicas hold.

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

feedback.answered: The Candidate's discriminator is resolved on sources: no legal history in the captured snapshot establishes the branch premise. A replica that receives PreAccept can hold Status >= ACCEPTED with Cmds == nil only if some local transition sets ACCEPTED, COMMITTED or EXECUTED without also installing commands. handleAccept stores bal, vbal, Seq and Deps but never writes Status, so an acceptor that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE even though it holds accepted attributes (S11-handleAccept). Every transition that does set Status >= ACCEPTED also sets Cmds in the same handler: handlePreAccept stores the received command when it sets PREACCEPTED/PREACCEPTED_EQ (S9-handlePreAccept), the leader-side accept and commit paths set inst.Cmds from lb.cmds (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S12-handleAcceptReply, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply), and handleCommit copies commit.Command (S13-handleCommit). formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

selections.rationale: Feedback-only product that narrows the active Candidate's exposure using source structure, without changing any map object. Comparing how the leader's and the peer's dependency vectors are computed shows why the N<=3 Thrifty equality exemption is sound in the owner-led case and why the recovery-led case is the one that can split: a peer recomputes with updateAttributes starting from the leader's transmitted deps vector and only increases components, and it skips the instance owner's row, so with a single fast-quorum peer the merged vector (componentwise maximum) equals that peer's vector whenever the leader is also the owner, and the leader installs that same merged vector on commit. When the leader is not the owner (recovery sub-case 5/6 restarts phase 1 for another replica's instance), the leader and the peer each skip the owner's row but add their own knowledge to their own rows, so the leader can contribute a component on the leader's row that the peer lacks while the peer contributes one on a different row: the merged vector is then strictly greater than both records and is held only by the leader after its fast commit.

feedback.answered: The exemption's reachable window is now located on sources. updateAttributes only raises the dependency components it is given: it starts from the received deps vector, skips the row of the instance owner named in the message, and for every other row raises deps[q] to the highest conflicting instance known locally (S7-attributes). A pre-accepting peer therefore returns a vector that dominates the leader's transmitted vector componentwise; with one peer (N=3, Thrifty, FastQuorumSize-1 = 1) the leader's merge equals that peer's vector, and the fast-commit branch installs the merged vector into the leader's own record (S10-handlePreAcceptReply). In that owner-led case the committed vector is held at the same vbal by both members of the fast quorum, so a recovery quorum (SlowQuorumSize = 2) must intersect one of them and sees the committed vector. The exemption is therefore not automatically unsafe. The case that can split is a phase 1 restarted for an instance whose owner is another replica (handlePrepareReply sub-case 5 or 6 calls startPhase1 with PreAccept.Replica = owner and LeaderId = recovering replica, S15-handlePrepareReply, S8-handlePropose-startPhase1). There the leader and the peer both skip the owner's row but raise their own rows from their own conflict tables, so the leader can contribute a component on its own row that the peer does not have while the peer contributes another: the merged vector is then strictly greater than either record and is held only by the committing leader, while the peer keeps its smaller vector at the same ballot (S9-handlePreAccept, S10-handlePreAcceptReply).

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.
